findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC3 assert the mechanism on Windows: the child's `rootdir:` header names the test file's directory, or the `ntpath` unit tests run in the Windows job. Prefer a run on the PR branch over a post-merge-only run.

Observation: "The same test passed in the sweep of run 44526811291 ... one hour earlier."
findings.finding: AC3 relies on one green `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix. The failure is an intermittent race: the same test passed one hour before the failing run with no fix. A single pass is therefore equally consistent with the bug still being present. The criterion can also only be evaluated after merge, and nothing checks that the new code path (the `--rootdir` pin) actually took effect on Windows.
scenarios: The fix is mis-wired on Windows (e.g. containment misfires and `[]` is returned), the race simply doesn't fire that run, and AC3 is signed off green.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC3 so it checks the mechanism on Windows. For example: "A `sweep (windows)` run including this change (workflow_dispatch on the PR branch, or the first main run after merge) shows the child pytest header `rootdir: C:\...\pytest-of-runneradmin\...` for the nested tests in test_fixture_env_repr_security.py, and those tests pass. The run id is recorded on the ticket." Optionally, also note that recurrence is monitored across the next N sweeps.

findings.finding: AC3 accepts a single green `sweep (windows)` run as proof of the fix. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that relative arguments are joined to the child cwd (`pathmod.join(cwd, arg)`) before `exists`/`isdir`, that any existing relative argument counts as 'under the cwd' (so it returns []), and add a mixed relative+absolute unit case.
evidence: Plan: 'It applies pytest's own `get_dirs_from_args` rule, so it sees exactly the paths pytest would'
run_nested_pytest runs the child with `cwd=cwd` (tests/_nested_pytest.py:83), which may differ from the parent's cwd (e.g. cwd=tmp_path callers).
findings.finding: The plan says the pin sees 'exactly the paths pytest would', but the existence check uses the parent process's `os.path.exists`. For relative arguments, pytest resolves against the CHILD's cwd (`absolutepath` in the child process), while the helper would resolve against the parent's cwd. The rule '[] if any one lies under the cwd' also only clearly covers absolute arguments. When a relative argument that exists in the child's cwd is mixed with an absolute out-of-cwd argument, the outcome is undefined.
findings.location: Approach — 'each argument not starting with `-`, cut at `::`, that exists on disk' and 'returns [] if no argument is an absolute existing path, or if any one lies under the cwd'
scenarios: A caller passes cwd=some_dir together with a relative 'sub/test_a.py' and an absolute out-of-cwd file. pytest counts the relative one (it is under cwd, so native behaviour should be kept), but the helper's parent-cwd exists() may miss it and apply a pin pytest would not have chosen.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise every candidate as `pathmod.normpath(pathmod.join(cwd, part))` before calling the injected `exists`/`isdir`, and treat any argument that was originally relative and exists as being under cwd.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either pin `--confcutdir` (not `--rootdir`) to the computed directory so only the collection or conftest boundary moves, or skip the pin when an ini candidate exists in the argument's ancestors; then correct the 'pins what a macOS run already gets' claim and add a test with an ini above the test file.
evidence: Plan root-cause step 2: the failing walk is driven by `_is_in_confcutdir` in Session.collect. The bug depends on confcutdir, not on rootdir itself.

Plan: confcutdir falls out of rootdir only because no ini file is found ('Rootdir and confcutdir become the repo'). When an ini is found, pytest takes confcutdir from inipath.parent and --rootdir no longer controls it.
Behaviour-change measurement covers only the 19 existing modules ('223 passed, 2 skipped'), not a caller that writes an ini above its test file.
findings.finding: Pinning `--rootdir` overrides the rootdir pytest takes from an ini file in the argument's ancestors. The plan's claim 'This pins what a macOS run already gets' is therefore wrong whenever the caller's tree has a pytest.ini/pyproject.toml/tox.ini/setup.cfg above the argument's directory. Natively, rootdir would be the ini's directory. With the pin it becomes the file's directory, while inipath and confcutdir stay at the ini. Node ids, the reported rootdir, and other rootdir-relative output then change. Pinning `--confcutdir` to the same directory would bound the collection walk (the only thing the bug needs) and leave rootdir and ini handling as pytest decides.
findings.location: Approach — 'otherwise it returns `--rootdir` = `pathmod.commonpath` of those directories' / 'This pins what a macOS run already gets'
scenarios: A nested test writes tmp_path/pytest.ini and tmp_path/sub/test_x.py and passes the absolute file path. Natively rootdir is tmp_path and the node id is 'sub/test_x.py::t'. With the pin, rootdir is tmp_path/sub and the node id is 'test_x.py::t', so a future caller asserting node ids or rootdir output breaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Return `["--confcutdir", <dir>]` from the helper (still returning [] when the caller passes --rootdir/-c/--config-file/--confcutdir). Session.collect then starts at <dir>, and pytest's own rootdir/ini resolution is unchanged. Keep the end-to-end test with a raising conftest.py in the shared ancestor, since it still proves the boundary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Check in `_pytest/config/__init__.py` (9.0.3/9.2.0) which argument list `determine_setup` receives, cite the line, and either fix the 'option values' rule to match or add a test with a known option whose value is an existing absolute path.
evidence: Plan: "It applies pytest's own `get_dirs_from_args` rule, so it sees exactly the paths pytest would ... pytest makes the same choice for option values (such as the value after `-k`), and such a value only counts if it is an existing absolute path."
Every other pytest claim in the plan carries a file:line citation; this one has none.
Testing covers only `-k expr` (not a path), so a known option whose value is an existing absolute path (e.g. `--basetemp X`, `--junitxml X`) is never tested.
findings.finding: The plan asserts, without citing source, that "pytest makes the same choice for option values (such as the value after `-k`)", meaning `get_dirs_from_args` sees option values as candidate paths. In pytest, `determine_setup` usually receives the parsed `file_or_dir` positionals plus *unknown* args, not the values of known options like `-k`. If so, the helper's rule of counting existing absolute option values does not match pytest's, and the 'it sees exactly the paths pytest would' guarantee does not hold.
scenarios: A caller passes a known option whose value is an existing absolute directory outside cwd (e.g. `--rootdir`-like or plugin options with path values). The helper counts it toward `commonpath`, but pytest does not, so the pinned rootdir differs from what pytest would choose on its own.

findings.finding: The end-to-end regression test needs the child's cwd and test file to share a writable, non-root ancestor holding a `conftest.py`. That only works if the cwd is set inside tmp_path. The plan never says whether `run_nested_pytest` already accepts a `cwd` override; the stated default is the repo. Otherwise, with or without `--rootdir`, pytest sets confcutdir to the ini file's directory, the ancestor conftest is still loaded, and the test fails after the fix. The plan itself measures a run 'under the checkout's own basetemp', where the repo's `pyproject.toml` would be found.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the separate option-value rule: treat every non-dash token exactly as `get_dirs_from_args` does (cut at `::`, resolve relative to cwd, keep if it exists), and add a mixed `-v <relpath> <abs C: path>` test expecting `[]`.

"pytest makes the same choice for option values (such as the value after `-k`), and such a value only counts if it is an existing absolute path."
findings.finding: The argument rule contradicts itself and is under-specified. The plan says the helper sees 'exactly the paths pytest would', which in `get_dirs_from_args` means every non-dash token resolved against cwd. It then says an option value 'only counts if it is an existing absolute path', which departs from pytest's rule for relative existing tokens. The plan also does not say how the helper would recognise a token as an option value rather than a positional argument without knowing each option's arity: `-v tests/x.py` vs `-k expr`.
scenarios: Args `-v tests/unit/x.py C:\...\y.py`. If `tests/unit/x.py` is treated as the value of `-v`, the in-repo rule ('any one lies under the cwd → []') never fires, and the helper pins rootdir to C: although pytest would see a repo path.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the option-value sentence with: "Every token not starting with `-` is cut at `::`, made absolute against cwd, and kept if it exists, exactly as get_dirs_from_args does. A relative existing token therefore resolves under cwd and yields `[]`. A non-existent token such as a `-k` expression is dropped."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Check pytest's issue tracker for the Windows cross-drive rootdir case and the `samefile_nofollow` lstat race (e.g. issue #14864 on the same fallback), cite what exists or file an issue, and add a removal condition for `_rootdir_pin` tied to the upstream fix.
evidence: Plan: "`commonpath` (`_pytest/pathlib.py`) catches the `ValueError` ... and returns `None`, so the common ancestor stays the cwd." and "each scanned entry ... goes through `samefile_nofollow(node.path, matchparts[0])`, which calls `p1.lstat()`".

Web search retrieved pytest-dev/pytest issue #14864, '(Windows) passing a file path collects the whole suite, on a network...', whose snippet says the culprit is `samefile_nofollow()`, 'which Session.collect() falls back to on Windows when two paths don't compare equal'. The same Windows fallback is already an active upstream topic.
The pytest docs source (docs.pytest.org `_pytest/main.html`, retrieved) shows that fallback was added for Windows short paths (#11895).
No mention of upstream status, a pytest version that fixes it, or a plan to report it.
findings.finding: The plan diagnoses two upstream pytest behaviours: on Windows, a cross-drive cwd/argument pair makes rootdir and confcutdir the cwd, so collection walks from the drive root; and `samefile_nofollow` calls `lstat` on sibling entries without tolerating concurrent removal. It never checks for or cites upstream pytest issues or fixes, and does not say whether an upstream report or fix would let the local workaround go away.
scenarios: A later pytest release fixes the cross-drive rootdir or makes `samefile_nofollow` tolerate a vanished entry, and the local pin stays behind as dead complexity with no removal trigger.
The same race hits a pytest launch that bypasses the helper (the plan names pytester and console-script runs as out of scope), and nobody has reported it upstream.

findings.finding: The plan says the rule counts 'each argument … that exists on disk', using injected `exists`/`isdir` that default to os.path.exists/isdir. For a relative argument those check against the PARENT process's cwd, not the `cwd` the child runs in. pytest resolves relative arguments against the child's invocation dir. So the claim to see 'exactly the paths pytest would' fails for every caller whose cwd differs from the parent's.
findings.location: Approach — '_rootdir_pin(args, cwd, *, pathmod=os.path, exists=os.path.exists, isdir=os.path.isdir)' / 'each argument not starting with `-`, cut at `::`, that exists on disk'
scenarios: A relative arg exists only under the child's cwd. The pin reads it as non-existent, which happens to give [], but only by accident.

A relative arg happens to exist relative to the parent's cwd too (for example 'tests/unit') while the child's cwd is elsewhere. The pin counts the wrong path, and the 'lies under the cwd' check uses a path the child never sees.
findings.suggested_fix: In _rootdir_pin, treat a relative argument as pathmod.join(cwd, part) for exists/isdir and containment (matching pytest's absolutepath against invocation_dir), or explicitly classify any relative argument as 'under cwd' and return [].

"otherwise it returns `--rootdir` = `pathmod.commonpath` of those directories, or `[]` when they are on different drives"

findings.finding: The Approach claims to 'Fix the class' in the sanctioned launcher. Yet three branches the plan specifies still produce the failing Windows layout: 'any one lies under the cwd → []', 'different drives → []', and an unguarded `commonpath` that can resolve to a drive root such as `C:\`. (1) A caller passing one in-repo path plus one %TEMP% path gets no pin. confcutdir stays on D:, and collection of the C: argument still starts at `C:\` and lstats %TEMP% siblings. (2) Arguments on two drives get no pin, with the same effect for the C: argument. (3) Two C: directories whose only common ancestor is `C:\` (or %TEMP% itself) pin rootdir there, so collection again scans the shared temp. The plan neither states that none of the 19 calling modules produce these argument mixes, nor tests or guards these residual paths.
scenarios: A future nested test passes both a repo conftest/plugin path and a tmp_path test file. On Windows it silently gets no pin and can hit the same FileNotFoundError race.
Arguments from two unrelated C: locations give commonpath `C:\`. rootdir and confcutdir become the drive root, and collection walks `C:\Users\...\Temp` again.
